from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Any complex wave is a sum of simple pieces.",
            "Like vectors, we decompose signals into basic parts.",
            "Think of a chord resolved into individual notes."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites & Intuition", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Load asset and show label
        piano = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/piano.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(piano, 'B2', scale_factor=0.3)
        label1 = Text("Fourier Series", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label1, 'B4', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(piano), Write(label1))
        
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * x), x_range=[-1, 1], color=GREEN)
        self.place_in_area(wave, 'A4', 'B6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(wave))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GREEN))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Morph the wave function into a sum of sines. Color: #FF00FF.
        sum_of_sines = VGroup(*[
            FunctionGraph(lambda x, n=n: (0.5/(n)) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * n * x), x_range=[-1, 1], color=PURPLE)
            for n in range(1, 4)
        ])
        harp = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/harp.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(harp, 'E2', scale_factor=0.3)
        
        self.place_in_area(sum_of_sines, 'D4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Transform(wave.copy(), sum_of_sines), FadeIn(harp))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(PURPLE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Just highlight the last line
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The series formula represents a signal's structure.",
            "The constant term is the average height.",
            "Summing sine waves creates complex oscillations."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Pure Fourier Series", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the general formula for Fourier Series.
        formula = MathTex(
            "f(x) = \\frac{a_0}{2} + \\sum_{n=1}^{\\infty} (a_n \\cos(nx) + b_n \\sin(nx))",
            color=WHITE
        )
        # Applying the fix from issue 37: self.place_in_area(formula, 'B2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "B2", "F5", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight the constant term a0/2.
        # Use sub-mobject indexing to find the a0 term
        a0_term = formula[0][2:7]
        
        self.play(
            Indicate(a0_term, color="#00FFFF"),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF")
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the frequency components (an, bn).
        an_term = formula[0][14:17]
        bn_term = formula[0][22:25]
        
        highlight_freq = VGroup(an_term, bn_term)
        
        self.play(
            highlight_freq.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00")
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Calculating Coefficients (1:45-3:15)", [
            "We use integrals to extract specific weights.",
            "The overlap measures how much frequency exists.",
            "Think of a filter tuning to a frequency."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        radio_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/radio.svg")
        filter_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/filter.svg")
        
        formula = MathTex(r"a_n = \frac{2}{T} \int_0^T f(t) \sin\left(\frac{2\pi n t}{T}\right) dt", color=WHITE)
        projection = VGroup(
            Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.4),
            FunctionGraph(lambda t: np.sin(t*2), x_range=[0, 4], color=RED)
        )
        coeff_text = Text("a_n = 0.5", color=GREEN, font_size=36)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Use assets as requested
        group1 = VGroup(formula, radio_icon.scale(0.5)).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.place_in_area(group1, 'B1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.85)))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visual Synthesis & Application", [
            "Building a square wave reveals hidden complexity.",
            "Stacking waves makes the shape sharper.",
            "More frequencies lead to better approximations."
        ])
        
        # Assets
        oscillator = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/oscillator.svg")
        speaker = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speaker.svg")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show three sine waves stacking together using the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/oscillator.svg] as the source. Color: #FF00FF.
        wave1 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(x), x_range=[-PI, PI])
        wave2 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.3 * np.sin(3*x), x_range=[-PI, PI])
        wave3 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.2 * np.sin(5*x), x_range=[-PI, PI])
        
        waves = VGroup(wave1, wave2, wave3).set_color("#FF00FF")
        oscillator_icon = self.place_at_grid(oscillator, "A2", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(waves, "A4", "C6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(waves), FadeIn(oscillator_icon))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF00FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Demonstrate the emergence of a square wave. Color: #00FFFF.
        # Note: Do not use always_redraw for complex/heavy mobjects as per instructions.
        # We will manually transform/create the square wave.
        def square_wave_func(x):
            return 0.5 * np.sin(x) + 0.3 * np.sin(3*x) + 0.2 * np.sin(5*x)

        sum_wave = FunctionGraph(square_wave_func, x_range=[-PI, PI]).set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.place_in_area(sum_wave, "D4", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Transform(waves, sum_wave))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the convergence at discontinuities to produce an output signal via [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speaker.svg]. Color: #FFFF00.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        speaker_icon = self.place_at_grid(speaker, "D2", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(speaker_icon))
        
        dot = Dot(color="#FFFF00").move_to(sum_wave.point_from_proportion(0.5))
        self.play(Flash(dot))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Fourier series maps signals to frequency coefficients.",
            "This is vital for MP3s and images.",
            "Our ears use this to interpret sound."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Wrap-up", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        waves = VGroup(
            *[FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(k * x), x_range=[-2, 2], color=BLUE_D).shift(UP * 0.2 * k) for k in range(1, 4)]
        )
        # Using SVGMobject for the assets
        mp3_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mp3.svg")
        ear_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ear.svg")
        
        # Positioning via grid
        self.place_at_grid(waves, 'B3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(mp3_icon, 'D4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(ear_icon, 'F4', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        mp3_label = Text("MP3/JPEG", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).next_to(mp3_icon, RIGHT)
        ear_label = Text("Ear/Cochlea", font_size=20, color=GREEN).next_to(ear_icon, RIGHT)

        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeIn(waves))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeIn(mp3_icon), Write(mp3_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeIn(ear_icon), Write(ear_label))
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Magic of Pure Fourier Series: Breaking Down Waves

sections.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Briefly review the concept of a 'vector basis' (e.g., i, j, k axes). Introduce the core philosophy: any complex periodic signal can be decomposed into simple, pure sine and cosine 'building blocks'. Visualize this as a musical chord being resolved into individual notes.
sections.example: Imagine a color: purple is actually a mixture of pure red and pure blue. Fourier series is the 'prism' that splits the signal color into its pure primary components.

sections.title: Defining the Pure Fourier Series (0:45-1:45)
sections.content: Present the mathematical definition: f(x) = a₀/2 + Σ(aₙ cos(nx) + bₙ sin(nx)). Explain the function of each part: the average value (a₀), and the contribution of higher-frequency ripples (aₙ, bₙ).
sections.example: Visual animation: A circle rotating (phasor) that draws a wave. Show how changing 'n' adds high-frequency 'wiggles' to the curve.

sections.title: Calculating Coefficients (1:45-3:15)
sections.content: Introduce the Orthogonality Principle. Explain that we extract the specific weight of each sine/cosine by calculating the area of overlap (integral) between the signal and the basis function. Use a 'Filtering' metaphor.
sections.example: A 'tuning fork' analogy: The integral acts like a filter that only rings when it finds the specific frequency n. If the signal doesn't contain that frequency, the overlap is zero.

sections.title: Visual Synthesis & Application (3:15-4:30)
sections.content: Demonstrate the 'Reconstruction'. Show an animation of a Square Wave being formed by stacking successive sine waves. As 'n' increases, the approximation gets sharper.
sections.example: A digital synthesizer or audio equalizer: Each slider (fader) on an equalizer represents one 'aₙ' or 'bₙ' coefficient. Moving the fader changes the 'texture' of the sound wave.

sections.title: Summary & Wrap-up (4:30-5:00)
sections.content: Reinforce that Fourier series turns complex time-domain signals into simple frequency-domain coefficients. It is the backbone of MP3 compression, image processing (JPEG), and quantum mechanics.
sections.example: A cat listening to a complex noise—its brain (via the cochlea) performs a Fourier transform to identify the specific purrs and meows hidden in the air pressure fluctuations.
